title: Edge-side structured-log gateway with adaptive field bucketing and deterministic corrid mapping
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: High-cardinality and tenant-specific fields in structured logs are causing Loki index cost spikes, inconsistent correlation across proxies, and a noisy developer experience when tracing requests. We need a lightweight edge-side gateway that normalizes and enriches structured logs, performs deterministic correlation-id (corrid) mapping across tenants, and applies adaptive bucketing on high-cardinality keys before they hit central ingestion. Goal: reduce Loki index cardinality and downstream storage cost by 30% for top-10 noisy services while preserving traceability and deterministic linkability between logs and spans.
acceptance_criteria: Edge sidecar (WASM or Go) deployed as a DaemonSet in test cluster that accepts JSON log payloads and forwards to Loki/ELK-compatible write endpoint
Adaptive bucketing rules implemented: numeric quantization, categorical top-K passthrough + hashed bucket for tail values; configurable per-tenant and per-route
Deterministic corrid mapping: tenant-scoped HMAC-based salt config so same incoming corrid maps to stable tenant-scoped id across restarts
Zero-copy enrichment path: attach trace/span link metadata without reserializing entire payload for common cases
End-to-end test demonstrating 30% reduction in Loki label cardinality for selected noisy service without breaking existing trace joins
Dashboard panels for: per-tenant cardinality, top N high-cardinality fields, write amplification, sidecar CPU/mem, and dropped/normalized field counts
Migration plan for rolling index rekeys with canary and rollback steps documented and validated in staging
infra_changes: Add sidecar Helm chart with feature flags for bucketing strategies
Expose tenant salt KMS secret mount for deterministic HMAC mapping
Add per-tenant sampling and backpressure tokens in gateway config
Schema migration job to remap legacy label keys to new bucketed keys for index compaction
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged rollout to internal staging for 2 services (1 day)
2) Canary to 5% of traffic for two noisy services with cardinality/trace checks (3 days)
3) Gradual ramp to 50% with monitoring; if cardinality reduction < target, pause and iterate (4 days)
4) Full rollout tenant-by-tenant with coordinated index compaction windows (customer-facing tenants scheduled during off-peak)
metrics_and_dashboards: ingest.sidecar.buckets.created - histogram of created bucket ids
loki.index.cardinality.per_label - derived panel aggregating unique label cardinality
trace.join.success.rate - percentage of logs that link back to spans after mapping
ingest.sidecar.cpu_usage and mem_usage for resource budgeting
notes: 2026-02-18: Spike completed; prototype using a small Go sidecar replaced earlier heavy python transformer. WASM experiment promising for on-host minimal footprint.
2026-02-20: Trade-off: exact-pass-through vs hashed-bucket. Decided to preserve top-K values and hash all others to reduce dev impact and preserve debugging for the common cases.
2026-02-21: Security: HMAC salt per-tenant must be rotated via KMS and never written to logs. KMS integration required (see infra_changes).
2026-02-23: Backpressure: sidecar will implement a local LRU buffer with bounded size and a 'slow-path' to append count-only placeholders for overloaded ingestion to avoid tail-latency spikes.
2026-02-24: ELK compatibility shim to retain existing processing pipelines by emitting a compatible set of fields; tests failing on nested array flattening — assigned to ENG-100999 for helper util
